pairs.question: At quae in loca, et quo versum, lumen hoc diffunditur?
pairs.answer: In corpora generis secundi, et generis etiam tertii, diaphana, et opaca, et in lucida quoque generis primi.
pairs.derivation: Question is the closing interrogative of the first content paragraph; the author answers it as the opening sentence of the next paragraph. Answer cut at the first full stop; what follows ('Sed in omnia proprio quodam modo...') elaborates the manner of diffusion and is not part of the direct answer.

pairs.question: An aeris profunditas, eam reddit apparentiam?
pairs.answer: Ita videtur, ut scilicet in magna distantia, ob multarum sui partium interiectionem, ac mutuam subitionem, opacitatis aliquas sumat vices.
pairs.derivation: Author asks whether the depth of air produces the blue appearance of the sky; he answers himself 'Ita videtur, ut...'. Answer cut at the first full stop; what follows ('Hoc enim proprii muneris habet aer...') is supporting elaboration, not the direct answer.

pairs.question: Cur autem in fornicis modum visitur?
pairs.answer: Quia circumquaque ab aequali invervallo, oculos nostros incurrunt quasi in centrum, partes illae aeris omnes, opacitatem eam referentes.
pairs.derivation: Author asks why the sky-color is seen in the shape of an arch; he answers with 'Quia...'. Answer cut at the first full stop; what follows ('Hanc ob causam opacitatem in aere efformari...') turns to corroborating evidence and is not part of the direct answer.
